The graph represents the function $y=\frac{a}{x-b}+k.$ What is the value of $a+b+k?$
worked_solution:
First, notice that the horizontal asymptote of the graph is $y=0.5,$ while the vertical asymptote is $x=3.$ This means that $k=0.5$ and $b=3,$ and we can re-write our function as

$$
y=\frac{a}{x-3}+0.5.
$$

Also, we are given that the point $(1,1.5)$ lies on the graph. Substituting its coordinates into the equation above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{a}{x-3}+0.5 \\ 1.5 & =\frac{a}{1-3}+0.5 \\ 1 & =\frac{a}{-2} \\ a & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $a+b+k=-2+3+0.5=1.5.$
